note: Hebrew kushit is "Cushite"; Cush usually means the Nile region south of Egypt (Nubia, the Septuagint's "Ethiopia"), but some identify it with Cushan near Midian (Hab 3:7), so the bare gentilic is safer.

kjv: who [is] faithful in all mine (Yahweh's) house
mine: he (Moses) is entrusted with all My (Yahweh's) house
note: Hebrew ne'eman can mean "faithful/reliable" or "entrusted (with)"; both are defensible, the latter fits the household-steward image.
Hebrew mar'eh "(in) plain sight"; in 1611 "apparently" meant "manifestly, openly", while today it means "seemingly", the opposite nuance.
